rationale: Recent global-anchor and carry-refresh variants failed hard, but the reverse-tail curriculum itself is still the strongest local motif. This edit keeps the same recurrent-tail family and compile-stable step structure, while changing only what the carry path targets: each recurrent tail block now pulls toward its own first-pass decoder activation instead of a single final decoder anchor. The hypothesis is that block-local anchors preserve the winning reverse-tail reuse while reducing over-smearing in the late recurrent path and surviving int8 roundtrip better than the decoder-output anchor.
title: Block-Local Reverse-Tail Anchors
